flags.item: The published 'ATS coin-flip test' cannot fail
flags.detail: data/derived/luck.json reports n=13784, wins=6892, rate=0.5 and p vs 50% = 1.0. The sample is built as x concatenated with -x (scripts/analyze_luck.py pools ats_margin and its negation, and verification/recompute.py lines 195-205 reproduce it), so exactly one of each pair is positive: rate = 0.5 and p = 1.0 for every possible dataset. It is presented as evidence that 'the spread market shows no exploitable tilt', which it does not test. The one-sided version, one observation per game, is n=6892, home covers=3371, rate=0.4891, 95% Wilson CI (0.477326, 0.500922), two-sided p=0.072687.
flags.action: Relabel the pooled figure as an arithmetic identity or replace it with the one-sided test before it is cited again. Until then no tilt conclusion can be drawn from it in either direction.

flags.item: The sign diagnostic compares two different formulae, not two hypotheses
flags.detail: Both branches reproduce (0.4891 and 0.6003). But if spread_line is the home team's expected margin (the convention the repository proves elsewhere with corr=0.43 and the moneyline cross-check), then result+spread_line is not 'the other sign convention'. Writing m for the home margin and h for the handicap, m + (-h) = m - h; the second expression is m + h, which is h's own negation, so a 60% 'cover rate' is what you get whenever the home team's margin is near zero relative to a large line. Evidence for the sign convention should come from the moneyline cross-check, not this ratio.
flags.action: Keep the moneyline cross-check; either drop the 0.6003 branch or describe it as the complement. Do not cite 0.6003 as a betting result.

flags.item: Published correlation sample does not reproduce from the committed extract
flags.detail: 3 entries in the project's own verification record are marked 'DIFFERS (expected)'. The site discloses that the four-leg parlay n is 7,560 while a checkout recomputes 6,024, because the extract was pruned to a different season window than the one used for the published coefficients. The sign and magnitude of the correlation reproduce; the n does not.
flags.action: Re-run the analysis against the committed extract, or label the published n as the pre-pruning window.

flags.item: The official injury-policy page cited by the root site returns 404
flags.detail: data/sources.json id 'nfl-injury-policy' points at https://operations.nfl.com/football-ops/league-governance/injury-report/, re-checked 2026-11-12: HTTP 404 ('404 - FLAG ON THE PLAY'). The root site therefore blocks injury signals. The league's live injury report itself (https://www.nfl.com/injuries/) DOES serve Week 10 of the 2026 season and is the feed used by decision-hub's own tracker, so the data availability claim is now out of date even though the policy document is still missing.
flags.action: Cite the live report for data and stop asserting that no injury source is available; keep the policy-PDF gap as an open item. See decision-hub/pages/injuries.html for the working tracker.

flags.item: No page states whether a missing starter is replaced by a 2nd/3rd/4th-string player
published_where: pages/signals.html (root nav has no equivalent page)
flags.detail: The requirement is explicit: the system must know when a defense or offense is on its 2nd, 3rd or 4th string because starters are out. A grep of the repository finds no code that joins the injury report to a depth chart; the phrase appears only in prose. The nflverse depth_charts release does carry a per-snapshot rank (pos_rank) from the 2025 season onward, and decision-hub's tracker is the first code in this repository to use it.
flags.action: Publish depth lost per team-week from decision-hub/data/injuries.json; treat any strategy that assumes a backup's performance as unverified until it has a measured effect size.

flags.item: Leaderboard rewards are a schedule, not a funded pool
flags.detail: No prize money exists and no payout mechanism is verified. The reward tiers are a design proposal and are labelled as such on the root site.
